"Triple Red 7s Multiplier" has had no $77,777 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Every line of Triple Red 7s Multiplier's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
802.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

803.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Triple Red 777s" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of five still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Everything above about "Triple Red 777s" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
803.headline: Top prizes are still left

804.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Diamond Bingo" are sold. The top prize count has held, with five of seven still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Everything here about "Diamond Bingo" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 18.
804.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

805.body:
"Multiply Your Money" has gone over a month without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $50,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "Multiply Your Money" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
805.headline: No new top prize claims

806.body:
"Win $50, $100 or $200" is near the midpoint of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Every line of Win $50, $100 or $200's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
806.headline: Where this game is in its run

807.body:
On "Ravens X2", one $20,000 top prize was claimed earlier this week. That leaves two of the original four. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Everything here about "Ravens X2" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 18.
807.headline: Top prize count went down

808.body:
"Ravens X10" has three of four top prizes left and is in the middle of its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Tomorrow's count on "Ravens X10" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
808.headline: Tickets sold so far

809.body:
About a quarter of the tickets for "Gold Bar Bingo" are sold. The top prize count has held, with six of seven still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "Gold Bar Bingo" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
809.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

810.body:
"In the Green" is down to five top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed in this morning's update. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Everything above about "In the Green" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
810.headline: Someone claimed a $50,000 prize

811.body:
Extreme Green's prizes make it a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of the prize money still unclaimed, about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

The numbers for "Extreme Green" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
811.headline: How the prize money is divided

812.body:
On "Loose Change®", one $1,000 top prize was claimed earlier this week. That leaves fifteen of the original 24. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Tomorrow's count on "Loose Change®" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
812.headline: The top prize list got shorter

813.body:
One of The Price is Right™'s top prizes was claimed two weeks ago. A player in Maryland won $50,000. The game started with six top prizes and now has four top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

If "The Price is Right™" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
813.headline: Fewer $50,000 prizes left

814.body:
On "High Voltage", one $100,000 top prize was claimed in the latest numbers. That leaves six of the original eight. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Every line of High Voltage's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
814.headline: Another top prize was claimed

815.body:
A $100,000 top prize on "$100,000 Crossword" was claimed two weeks ago. The game started with nine top prizes and has eight top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The table below shows the full count for "$100,000 Crossword", with every prize level included.
815.headline: The top prize list got shorter

816.body:
"Deluxe Crossword" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $50,000 was claimed over a week ago. Unsold tickets still hold seven of the original eight. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

The numbers for "Deluxe Crossword" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
816.headline: A player won a top prize

817.body:
"Hello Money!" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $50,000 was claimed three days ago. Unsold tickets still hold six of the original seven. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

The numbers for "Hello Money!" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
817.headline: Top prize count went down

818.body:
The most common win left on "10X Cash" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $1,000, and 38 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The numbers for "10X Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
818.headline: A close look at the prizes

819.body:
"30X Cash" is near the start of its run, with most of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

The most common prize left on "30X Cash" right now is $30.

Everything above about "30X Cash" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
819.headline: How far along this game is

820.body:
"Cozy Cash" just went on sale in Maryland. The game has seven full prize levels with 35 top prizes of $500. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

Tomorrow's count on "Cozy Cash" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
820.headline: New game, all prizes left

821.body:
"Season's Greetings" has joined the Maryland lineup at $2 with six top prizes of $10,000. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

Everything above about "Season's Greetings" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
821.headline: Brand new, no claims yet

822.body:
"Peppermint Payout" just went on sale in Maryland. The game has nine full prize levels with six top prizes of $30,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

Tomorrow's count on "Peppermint Payout" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
822.headline: A brand-new game to watch

823.body:
"Holly-Day Cash" is new from the Maryland Lottery. It is a $5 game with seven top prizes of $50,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

The numbers for "Holly-Day Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
823.headline: First day on sale

824.body:
"Winter Multiplier" just reached Maryland stores with nine top prizes of $100,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

The table below shows the full count for "Winter Multiplier", with every prize level included.
824.headline: A new game is here

825.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Win $100, $200 or $500", nearly all are still unsold. The game is near the start of its run, with 12,777 of 12,822 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Tomorrow's count on "Win $100, $200 or $500" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
825.headline: Early stage or late
